problems.text: ov-sync writes straight to OpenViking, so a local folder has no way into the bucket that feeds the queue which paces, retries and dead-letters writes.
There is no way to choose which local files go to the bucket and under which prefix, short of copying `sync.py` and its folder list.
Nothing records which local files were sent to the bucket, so deletes cannot be mirrored and unchanged files would be re-sent.
The repo's gates cover Python and TypeScript only, so a Go module would ship unchecked.

goals.text: A local folder can be mirrored into a prefix of the ov-sync bucket with the CI action's manifest logic, so the queue and consumer can carry it to OpenViking.
A config file decides what is synced and where in the bucket it lands.

outcomes.change: `ovsq run` mirrors a folder into a bucket prefix using the action's manifest logic
outcomes.checked_by: Go tests against an in-process fake S3 (upload, unchanged second run, `--delete`, failed upload keeps its old manifest entry, manifest written after each batch, files under `_state/` never uploaded, `manifest.json` never written)

outcomes.change: `ov-sync-queue.toml` selects files and the target prefix
outcomes.checked_by: Go tests for loading, defaults, `OVSQ_` overrides, and refusing a prefix that is not `<owner>/<name>` or a bad `source`

outcomes.change: A local cache and a per-source bucket manifest record what was sent
outcomes.checked_by: Go tests showing a file with matching size and mtime is not re-hashed, a lost cache costs no re-upload when the manifest matches, and `status` makes no write

outcomes.change: The Go gates run with the repo's other gates, and the package is documented
outcomes.checked_by: `prek run --all-files` and `loopctl gate stamp` run `go vet` and `go test` for the module
